post.title: Inspection before payment
post.text:
Pipeline check only. Not for publication.

A Danish buyer signs a supply contract that says only "payment on delivery". When the goods arrive damaged, three lines are still missing: who inspects, how fast notice must go out, and whether the buyer may hold the price.

Write those lines before signature.

post.title: Kontrol før betaling
post.text:
En dansk virksomhed køber varer i et andet EU-land. Kontrakten siger kun "betaling ved levering". Hvis varen er beskadiget, mangler tre linjer: hvem der kontrollerer, hvor hurtigt der skal gives besked, og om køber må holde betalingen tilbage.

Skriv det ind før underskrift.

article.title: Currency and short payment
article.text:
Cross-border invoices often fail in the quiet lines, not in the headline price.

A Danish company invoices in euro. The buyer pays the figure on the invoice, and the seller still receives less, because the contract never said who carries intermediary bank charges or whether a short payment counts as late.

Before the next export or import contract is signed, read three clauses together:
• the currency and the amount that must arrive
• when delivery and risk move
• what a short or late payment allows the seller to do

script.title: Thirty seconds on inspection
script.text:
A contract that says only "payment on delivery" is not finished.

Say who inspects the goods, how many days notice of a defect must take, and whether the buyer may hold the price.

post.title: Law and venue
post.text:
Two EU companies sign, and the last page names no law and no court.

When a delivery fails, the first dispute is not the goods. It is which country's rules apply, and where a claim has to be filed.

Pick the governing law and the venue before signature. Then read the liability cap next to them, so a claim is not won in the wrong place.

post.title: Liability cap
post.text:
A liability cap that says "the price of this order" feels safe until the loss is the whole shipment, not the invoice line.

In an EU supply contract, write what the cap covers, what it never covers, and whether delay sits inside the cap or outside it.

I read that clause against the delivery terms before you sign.

article.title: Late performance
article.text:
Late performance is a clause, not a surprise.

An EU supply contract should say when the clock starts, how the other side gives notice, and which remedies stay available if the delay is short. Interest, suspension and termination do not belong in three different documents that contradict each other.

Put the notice address, the cure period and the remedy in the same section as the delivery date.

script.title: Thirty seconds on venue
script.text:
Before you sign a cross-border supply contract, read the last page out loud.

Which law applies? Which court hears a claim? Does the liability cap follow that same choice?

If any answer is missing, the draft is not ready.
